newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Marathon talks to end Colombian truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Marathon talks to end Colombian truckers' strike.

text.p: Marathon talks aimed at ending a six-day-old strike by Colombian truckers continued Friday morning, but a key union demand remained unresolved, negotiators said.

They said about 18 points on the list of demands put forward by the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC) had been settled in the talks that began at about 11 a.m. local time (1600 GMT) Thursday and were still going on at 7 a.m. (1200 GMT) Friday.
But there was still no agreement over the ACC's principal demand, for the government to set minimum cargo rates for highway freight.

"The only point that's left to be settled is the issue of cargo rates," Mario Quiroga, the ACC's sectional chief for central Boyaca province and a member of its strike barganing committee, told Reuters.

"It's not clear how soon this can be settled," he said, adding that in some cases government and union officials were arguing over differences that amount to as little as $1 in terms of overall freight charges.
"We're still in the same situation," Quiroga said, stressing that cargo rates were the main issue in the work stoppage that began at midnight Saturday.

The government declared the ACC strike illegal, with immediate effect from midnight Thursday, but Quiroga and other union officials said there was no news of any arrests, fines or penalties imposed against strikers as of Friday morning.
Jose Noe Rios, the government's deputy Labor Minister and chief negotiator with the truckers, told local radio he was confident the work stoppage would be lifted in the next few hours.
But he conceded that no agreement had been hammered out over the thorny issue of cargo rates.
